o.text:
Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish چین (çın), from Proto-Turkic *čïn (“true, real”), presumably borrowed from Sinitic 眞 (MC tsyin, “true, real”).
Cognate with Old Uyghur [script needed] (čïn, “true, real”); Tatar чын (çın), Kazakh шын (şyn), Uzbek chin, Khakas сын (sın), Tuvan шын (şın, “true, real”), etc.
Ultimately from Middle High German erbe (“heritage”), whence also German Erbe (“heritage”); via Polish herb (“coat of arms, emblem”), via Russian герб (gerb, “coat of arms”).
Ultimately from Arabic تَضْيِيق (taḍyīq). Cognate with Turkish tazyik, Uzbek tazyiq.
Borrowed from Persian زنجبیل (zanjabil), زنجفیل (zanjafil), from Sanskrit शृङ्गवेर (śṛṅgavera). Ultimately from Old Tamil.

From Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (şikence, “press”), [script needed] (işkenci, “pain, trouble”), from Persian شکنجه (šekanje, “torment; torture”), اشکنجه (eškanje). Cognates with Turkish işkence.
Borrowed from Russian фармакогнозия (farmakognozija). By surface analysis, farmako- + -qnoziya.
